about: Le Pauillac de Pichon Baron is the third wine of Château Pichon Baron, a Second Growth in the 1855 classification whose turreted château, built in 1851, faces Château Latour across the road at the southern edge of Pauillac. The estate goes back to 1694, when the Enclos Rauzan came into the Pichon Longueville family as a dowry. It was divided among heirs in 1850. AXA bought it in 1987, and Christian Seely has run it since the mid-2000s as head of AXA Millésimes.

The grand vin comes from the oldest vines on the historic plateau. Le Pauillac draws mainly on younger vines, including clay-limestone and gravel plots of the Tour Pibran vineyard, which the estate owns, between Pontet-Canet and Mouton Rothschild. The château’s own team picks, makes and ages it the same way as the senior wines. In recent vintages it has been mostly Merlot, about 80%, with Cabernet Sauvignon, aged about 12 months in barrels that have held wine before.

The estate makes Le Pauillac as an approachable wine to drink young. It is fruity, supple and balanced, with ripe plum and blackberry, soft tannins and a long finish, a gentler side of Pichon Baron that is ready now. It is a chance to taste one of Pauillac’s great names years before its grand vin would be ready, and the house style shows through: dark fruit, polish and a sense of place from the gravel slopes above the Gironde.
facts: Mostly Merlot with Cabernet Sauvignon (about 80/20 in 2020 and 2021)
Younger estate vines, including Tour Pibran
AOC Pauillac; third wine of a Second Growth (1855)
